items.en: The Same Pattern Across the Remaining Three Cultivations
items.zh: 正料揀事理兩修發禪不定 · 理修、事理修、非事非理修
parent: Distinguishing That Dhyāna's Arising Is Not Fixed

zh: 問曰：若事修乃發非事非理等諸禪三昧不共之法，並由先世習因而得者，則一切隨事而修，皆應得首楞嚴等諸禪三昧不共之法。若爾，何故一切十方諸佛殷勤稱歎般若波羅蜜？若能如聞，行者即具足一切佛法。答曰：此難更成今義。所以者何？若行者過去已經值無量諸佛，從諸佛所聞說般若波羅蜜，如聞而行，則今世隨有所修，一切非事非理諸禪三昧不共之法自然開發，若過去不聞般若，不修般若，今世雖聞雖修，而不能發，何況不聞不修而得發耶？復次，今世雖聞般若，雖修般若，而不得發，後世若值諸佛菩薩，聞說般若波羅蜜，如聞而行，即一切大乘諸禪三昧不共之法悉當開發，故知皆是聞般若，如聞而行能發，非無因緣。是以一切十方諸佛殷勤稱歎般若波羅蜜，若有如聞而行，則能具足一切佛法，正成今義。
en: Question: if phenomenal cultivation can bring forth unshared dharmas of neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-samādhi, all of it obtained through habituation-causes from former lives, then everyone who cultivates according to phenomenal practice ought to attain the Śūraṅgama and every other unshared dhyāna-samādhi as well. If this is so, why do all the buddhas of the ten directions so earnestly praise prajñā-pāramitā, saying that if a practitioner acts exactly as they have heard, they are thereby complete in every buddha-dharma? Answer: this challenge only further establishes the very point being made here. Why is this? If a practitioner has, in the past, already encountered measureless buddhas, heard prajñā-pāramitā expounded by them, and acted exactly as heard, then, in this present life, whatever is cultivated will bring forth every unshared dharma of neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-samādhi naturally, of itself. But if one did not hear prajñā in the past and did not cultivate prajñā, then, even hearing it and cultivating it in this present life, it cannot be brought forth — how much less could it be brought forth by neither hearing nor cultivating it at all? Furthermore: even if one hears prajñā and cultivates prajñā in this present life without it being brought forth, should one, in a future life, encounter buddhas and bodhisattvas, hear prajñā-pāramitā expounded, and act exactly as heard, then every unshared Mahāyāna dhyāna-samādhi will thereupon be brought forth in full — hence it is known that, in every case, it is hearing prajñā and acting exactly as heard that is able to bring it forth; this is never without its own cause and condition. This is precisely why all the buddhas of the ten directions so earnestly praise prajñā-pāramitā: if one acts exactly as one has heard, one becomes thereby complete in every buddha-dharma — and this precisely establishes the point made here.

zh: 復次，行者以般若波羅蜜方便力故，能於事修之中即具非事非理修，勇猛精進，常修習者，則能發一切非事非理諸禪三昧不共之法。問曰：此與前何別？答曰：是中應作四句料揀：一者、因強而緣弱；二者、因弱而緣強；三者、因緣俱強；四者、因緣俱弱。一、因強而緣弱，能發非事非理諸禪三昧不共之法，如前分別；二、因弱而緣強，能發非事非理諸禪三昧不共之法，即是今之所明；三、因緣俱強，能發非事非理諸禪三昧不共之法者，以前合今，即是其事，此人得法最勝；四、因緣俱弱者，則今世或發或不發，設得發禪，微羸淺薄，亦不牢固，多好退失，像末世中極上行人，只得如此。如上三句所明者，萬中或有一無一。
en: Furthermore: through the power of skillful means of prajñā-pāramitā, a practitioner is able, within phenomenal cultivation itself, to already be complete in neither-phenomenal-nor-principle cultivation — and, cultivating with courage and diligence, constant and unbroken, is thereby able to bring forth every unshared dharma of neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-samādhi. Question: how does this differ from what was said before? Answer: here, a fourfold distinction should be made: the cause strong but the condition weak; the cause weak but the condition strong; cause and condition both strong; and cause and condition both weak. First, the cause strong but the condition weak, able to bring forth unshared dharmas of neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-samādhi, is exactly as distinguished before. Second, the cause weak but the condition strong, able to bring forth the same, is precisely what has just been clarified here. Third, cause and condition both strong, able to bring forth the same: this combines the prior case with the present one exactly, and such a person attains the dharma in the most excellent way of all. Fourth, cause and condition both weak: in this present life, it may or may not be brought forth at all, and even if dhyāna is brought forth, it is feeble and shallow, not at all firm, and prone to regress — this is all that even the very best practitioners of this latter age generally attain. Of the three cases given above, one may find perhaps one such person in ten thousand, or perhaps none at all.

zh: 第二、次料揀理修發禪不定，亦有四種不同：一、自有行人安心體真理止，還發理中禪定，謂空、無相等一切理中諸禪三昧；二、自有行人安心理止，而但發事中禪定，謂根本禪、背捨一切事中諸禪三昧；三、自有行人安心理止，而具發事理禪定，謂根本禪、背捨、空、無相等一切事理諸禪三昧；四、自有行人安心理止，乃發非事非理禪定，謂自性禪等中道所攝一切諸禪三昧不共之法。廣分別諸禪相及料揀修發之義，類如初句中說。
en: Second, next distinguishing the unpredictable arising of dhyāna through principle cultivation: this likewise has four differing kinds. First, some practitioners, settling the mind in embodying-truth, principle stopping, bring forth dhyāna-concentration of principle in turn — namely every dhyāna-samādhi of principle among emptiness, signlessness, and the like. Second, some practitioners, settling the mind in principle stopping, bring forth only phenomenal dhyāna-concentration — namely every phenomenal dhyāna-samādhi among the root dhyānas, the liberations, and the rest. Third, some practitioners, settling the mind in principle stopping, bring forth both phenomenal and principle dhyāna-concentration together — namely every phenomenal-and-principle dhyāna-samādhi among the root dhyānas, the liberations, emptiness, signlessness, and the rest. Fourth, some practitioners, settling the mind in principle stopping, bring forth instead neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-concentration — namely every unshared dharma of middle-way-embracing dhyāna-samādhi among the samādhi of self-nature and the rest. The full distinguishing of these dhyāna-marks, and of the meaning behind their unpredictable cultivation and arising, follows the same pattern already given in the first case above.

zh: 第三、次料揀事理修，發禪不定，亦有四種不同：一、自有行人安心緣俗體真事理止，便還發事理禪定，謂根本禪、背捨、空、無相等一切事理諸禪三昧；二、自有行人安心事理止，而但發事中禪定，謂根本禪、背捨等一切事中諸禪三昧；三、自有行人安心事理止，而但發理中禪定，謂空、無相等一切理中諸禪三昧；四、自有行人安心事理止，乃發非事非理禪定，謂自性禪及中道所攝一切諸禪三昧不共之法。廣分別諸禪相及料揀修發之義，類如初諸句中說。第四、次料揀非事非理修，發禪不定，亦有四種不同：一、自有行人安心息二邊分別非事非理止，還發非事非理禪，謂自性禪等及中道所攝一切諸禪三昧不共之法；二、自有行人安心非事非理止，而但發事中禪定，謂根本禪、八背捨等一切事中諸禪三昧；三、自有行人安心非事非理止，而但發理中禪定，謂空、無相等一切理中諸禪三昧；四、自有行人安心非事非理止，而具發事理禪定，謂根本禪、背捨及空、無相等一切事理諸禪三昧。廣分別諸禪相及料揀修發之義，類如初句中說。
en: Third, next distinguishing the unpredictable arising of dhyāna through phenomenal-and-principle cultivation: this likewise has four differing kinds. First, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal-and-principle stopping that takes the conventional as its object while still embodying truth, bring forth phenomenal-and-principle dhyāna-concentration in turn, namely every phenomenal-and-principle dhyāna-samādhi among the root dhyānas, the liberations, emptiness, signlessness, and the rest. Second, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal-and-principle stopping, bring forth only phenomenal dhyāna-concentration, namely every phenomenal dhyāna-samādhi among the root dhyānas, the liberations, and the rest. Third, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal-and-principle stopping, bring forth only dhyāna-concentration of principle, namely every dhyāna-samādhi of principle among emptiness, signlessness, and the rest. Fourth, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal-and-principle stopping, bring forth instead neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-concentration, namely the samādhi of self-nature and every other unshared, middle-way-embracing dhyāna-samādhi. The full distinguishing of these dhyāna-marks, and of the meaning behind their unpredictable cultivation and arising, follows the same pattern already given in the earlier cases above.

Fourth, next distinguishing the unpredictable arising of dhyāna through neither-phenomenal-nor-principle cultivation: this likewise has four differing kinds. First, some practitioners, settling the mind in neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping that sets to rest the distinguishing of both extremes, bring forth neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna in turn, namely the samādhi of self-nature and every other unshared, middle-way-embracing dhyāna-samādhi. Second, some practitioners, settling the mind in neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping, bring forth only phenomenal dhyāna-concentration, namely every phenomenal dhyāna-samādhi among the root dhyānas, the eight liberations, and the rest. Third, some practitioners, settling the mind in neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping, bring forth only dhyāna-concentration of principle, namely every dhyāna-samādhi of principle among emptiness, signlessness, and the rest. Fourth, some practitioners, settling the mind in neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping, bring forth both phenomenal and principle dhyāna-concentration together, namely every phenomenal-and-principle dhyāna-samādhi among the root dhyānas, the liberations, emptiness, signlessness, and the rest. The full distinguishing of these dhyāna-marks, and of the meaning behind their unpredictable cultivation and arising, follows the same pattern already given in the first case above.

zh: 今但約止門中四修分別，則有十六種發禪不定。若更就觀門中四修分別，亦有十六種發禪不定。止觀合辨，則有三十二種發禪不定。此三十二但就法行人分別，若約信行人，聞說止觀教門發禪悟道不定，亦有三十二種，其事云云，今不具說。此一往通論，略出六十四種。若具約三乘人根性分別，則有一百九十二種發禪之異。若細歷諸禪，及約邪正辨發相分別，則有無量。今此皆是就行人心地分別，非是虛設之言。當知禪定發法不可思議，乃是諸佛菩薩境界，尚非二乘所量，豈是凡夫之所能測？若行者欲自行化他，必須少分識之，寧可謬自師心，則有自損損他之失，己所修治，為無慧利。
en: Here, distinguished only with reference to the four cultivations within the gate of stopping, there are sixteen kinds of unpredictable dhyāna-arising. If further distinguished with reference to the four cultivations within the gate of contemplation, there are likewise sixteen kinds of unpredictable dhyāna-arising. Taking stopping and contemplation together, there are thirty-two kinds of unpredictable dhyāna-arising in all. These thirty-two are distinguished only with reference to practitioners of the dharma-practice type; if one considers practitioners of the faith-practice type, whose dhyāna-arising and awakening to the path upon hearing the teaching-gate of stopping-and-contemplation expounded are likewise unpredictable, there are again thirty-two kinds — the matter being similar, it is not given here in full. Taken together in this general way, there are, in brief, sixty-four kinds in all. If distinguished fully according to the capacities of practitioners across the three vehicles, there are one hundred ninety-two differing kinds of dhyāna-arising. And if one traces through every dhyāna in fine detail, distinguishing the arising-marks in terms of the deviant and the correct as well, the number becomes measureless.

All of this, however, is distinguished strictly with reference to the practitioner's own state of mind — these are not idle words spoken without purpose. One should know that the dharma of dhyāna's arising is inconceivable, precisely the domain of buddhas and bodhisattvas, not even something the two lesser vehicles can fathom — how much less could an ordinary person hope to measure it? Should a practitioner wish to both practice and teach others, one must recognize at least some small part of this; to presume, in error, to set oneself up as one's own teacher instead would bring the fault of harming both oneself and others — and whatever cultivation one undertakes would then be without the benefit of true wisdom.

The escalating count here — 16, then 32 (adding contemplation to stopping), then 64 (adding the faith-practice type), then 192 (adding the three vehicles), then finally "measureless" — is itself the argument: the treatise is demonstrating, by simply continuing to subdivide, that any attempt to fix a one-to-one mapping between technique and result collapses under its own combinatorics. The distinction between "dharma-practice" and "faith-practice" practitioners (法行人 / 信行人) is a standard Abhidharma pairing — roughly, those who progress chiefly through their own contemplative effort versus those who progress chiefly through trust in the teaching as heard — and the humility of the closing lines is pointed: even the treatise's own elaborate sixteen-and-thirty-two-fold analysis is explicitly offered as only a partial map of something it calls, in the end, inconceivable.

quiz.q: If phenomenal cultivation can bring forth the Śūraṅgama and other unshared dharmas, why do the buddhas earnestly praise prajñā?
options: this only confirms the point: having heard prajñā and acted on it in the past, it arises now; without hearing and cultivating, it cannot
quiz.why: "This challenge only further establishes the very point being made here. Why is this? If a practitioner has, in the past, already encountered measureless buddhas, heard prajñā-pāramitā expounded by them, and acted exactly as heard, then, in this present life, whatever is cultivated will bring forth every unshared dharma ... naturally, of itself."

quiz.q: Among the four combinations of cause and condition, which attains the dharma most excellently, and which is what even the best practitioners of the latter age attain?
options: strong cause best; weak cause the latter age
both strong is most excellent; both weak is all the best latter-age practitioners attain
quiz.why: "Third, cause and condition both strong ... such a person attains the dharma in the most excellent way of all. Fourth, cause and condition both weak: in this present life, it may or may not be brought forth at all ... this is all that even the very best practitioners of this latter age generally attain."

quiz.q: Counting unfixed arisings across stopping and contemplation, faith- and dharma-practitioners, and the three vehicles, what totals does the text give?
options: sixteen for stopping, thirty-two with contemplation, sixty-four with faith-practitioners, one hundred ninety-two by the three vehicles
quiz.why: "Distinguished only with reference to the four cultivations within the gate of stopping, there are sixteen kinds ... Taking stopping and contemplation together, there are thirty-two ... in brief, sixty-four kinds in all. If distinguished fully according to the capacities of practitioners across the three vehicles, there are one hundred ninety-two differing kinds."
